Target audience: University students (Undergraduate level)

Section: section_1 — From Concrete to Abstract (0:00-1:00)

Lecture lines:
Vectors are more than just geometric arrows.
Consider vectors as abstract objects in sets.
These sets follow specific rules of engagement.
Linearity defines the structure of vector spaces.
Abstract spaces generalize our 2D/3D knowledge.

Planned animations:
Fade in a 2D vector arrow originating from the origin. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight the vector's components using dashed lines to the axes. (Color: #FF8080)
Animate the vector transformation by changing its head position. (Color: #80FF80)
Draw a grid and animate the vector as a point on the grid. (Color: #80FFFF)
Fade in the abstract notation 'v = (x, y)' near the vector. (Color: #FFFF80)

Section: section_2 — The Eight Axioms: The Rules of the Game (1:00-2:30)

Lecture lines:
Vector spaces require two fundamental operations.
Addition and scalar multiplication structure our space.
These operations must satisfy eight core axioms.
Polynomials follow these same algebraic rules.
Different structures obey identical structural laws.

Planned animations:
Display all 8 axioms as text on the screen. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Animate group by group, highlighting each with a subtle glow. (Color: #FF8080)
Show a visual example of the additive inverse axiom. (Color: #80FF80)

Section: section_3 — Beyond Arrows: Diverse Vector Spaces (2:30-4:00)

Lecture lines:
Vector spaces are surprisingly diverse structures.
Functions act as vectors in function spaces.
Adding functions mirrors geometric vector addition.

Planned animations:
Display a function graph next to a standard coordinate vector. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight the common structural properties between them. (Color: #FF8080)
Morph the arrow vector into the function curve. (Color: #80FF80)

Section: section_4 — The Power of Abstraction (4:00-5:00)

Lecture lines:
Abstraction provides a unified mathematical framework.
Properties proven once apply to all spaces.
Diverse systems share the same underlying logic.

Planned animations:
Show multiple disparate objects transforming into the same abstract shape. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Display the label 'Vector Space' hovering above them. (Color: #FF8080)
Fade out individual objects, leaving only the abstract structure. (Color: #80FF80)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Power of Abstraction", [
            "Abstraction provides a unified mathematical framework.",
            "Properties proven once apply to all spaces.",
            "Diverse systems share the same underlying logic."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        # Disparate objects: Matrix (Square), Polynomial (Curve), Signal (Wave)
        matrix = Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.1 * x**2, x_range=[-1, 1], color=YELLOW)
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(x * 3), x_range=[-1, 1], color=PURPLE)
        
        abstract_shape = Circle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        label = Text("Vector Space", color="#FF8080", font_size=24)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Show multiple disparate objects transforming into the same abstract shape."
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(curve, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(matrix), Create(curve), Create(wave))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(
            Transform(matrix, abstract_shape.copy()),
            Transform(curve, abstract_shape.copy()),
            Transform(wave, abstract_shape.copy())
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Display the label 'Vector Space' hovering above them."
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF8080"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Fade out individual objects, leaving only the abstract structure."
        self.play(FadeOut(matrix), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(wave))
        self.place_in_area(abstract_shape, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(abstract_shape))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#80FF80"))
        self.wait(2)
